clue.text: Calm after retreating journalist went off

indicators.note: after places the calm word behind the retreating journalist
retreating means going backwards, so the journalist's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
composed means calm and collected

explanation.surface: A newspaperman, once calm, flees and storms off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went off' reads as a departure but means rotted. ED, the editor, is the stock crossword journalist; 'retreating' reverses him and 'after' sets the calm word behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off has rotted, which is what decayed organic matter does.

clue.text: Marches taking up a number of days

indicators.note: taking up, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: some means a number of

explanation.surface: Protest marches lasting several days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses SOMED in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos are protest marches, short for demonstrations.

clue.text: Plant borders of Chinese territory in East

indicators.note: borders of means the outermost letters of the word Chinese

parts.note: land is territory

explanation.surface: A plant growing along the frontier of Chinese territory in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a small yellow-flowered plant of the buttercup and poppy families.

clue.text: Union negotiator

parts.note: it reads as a trade union official, but the union is a wedding, arranged by a matchmaker

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests labour talks; the union here is wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional matchmaker arranges weddings, so negotiates the union of couples.

clue.text: Keep going past contrary sailor in old hat

indicators.note: in places the reversed sailor inside the old hat word

parts.note: out means out of fashion, old hat

indicators.note: contrary means the other way, so the sailor word is reversed

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned seaman, going the opposite way, keeps sailing past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' is OUT, as in out of fashion; 'contrary' reverses the sailor, a SALT, to give TLAS for 'in' to place.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast is to survive longer than someone else, enduring beyond them.

clue.text: Most relaxed English afternoon break, last to start

indicators.note: last to start means the final letter moves to the front of the word

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: An English afternoon nap is the most restful thing of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to start' moves the A of SIESTA to its front, giving ASIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of easy, meaning most relaxed or comfortable.

clue.text: Some time, so to speak, for you and me

indicators.note: so to speak signals that a word is to be heard spoken, with its H silent

parts.note: hours are a period of some time

explanation.surface: An invitation to spend a while together, just the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' says HOURS is spoken, and its H is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to you and me is possessed by us both, the first person plural possessive pronoun.

clue.text: Extremist detected in unlawful trading

indicators.note: detected in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A radical caught in illegal dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone with extreme views, especially a political zealot.

clue.text: Asian gets a breath of air in Kent, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the breathing word inside the region

parts.note: Kent is a county in the South-East (SE) of England, so an example of it
inhales means takes in breath

explanation.surface: A visitor from Asia takes in fresh air in rural Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South-East England, giving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinhalese are the majority people of Sri Lanka, in South Asia.

clue.text: Division represented by lowly Republican in caucus

parts.note: simple means humble, lowly

indicators.note: in places the Republican inside the caucus word

parts.note: a faction is a caucus within a party

explanation.surface: Political division among a humble Republican within a party caucus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' sounds political but is arithmetic: one number divided by another.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction like three quarters shows one whole number divided by another, numerator over denominator.

clue.text: Defector in pursuit of spy, one going underground in Africa

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so the defector comes after the spy

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A turncoat chasing an agent who has gone into hiding on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going underground' sounds like a spy going to ground, but is meant literally: this burrowing rodent lives in African soil.
explanation.definitionFit: This hairless or furry rodent of Africa digs tunnels and lives beneath the soil.

clue.text: Singular protection for pugilist in love

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a mitten, like a boxing mitt, protects a boxer's hand

explanation.surface: A boxer whose only defence is lost because he has fallen for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smitten is struck with infatuation, deeply enamoured.

clue.text: Feline in revamped Disney corporation

indicators.note: in places the cat inside the reworked letters
revamped means remodelled, so the letters of Disney are rearranged

parts.note: a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cartoon cat inside a remodelled Disney company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' makes SYNDIE from the company name, and 'in' tucks the feline between its fifth and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of businesses or people combined for a commercial venture, much like a corporate body.

clue.text: Here the Spanish may meet Dad carrying short loaf

indicators.note: carrying means the father holds something inside him

parts.note: Pa is a familiar name for a father

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to loaf is to laze about

explanation.surface: Spaniards gather where a father is holding a small bread loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread but is the verb meaning idle; 'short' trims its final E, and 'carrying' has Dad hold what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square in a Spanish town, a natural place for people to gather.

clue.text: Restrictive level

definitions.meaning: binding, as a ... agreement constrains someone
drawing, making the scores equal in a game

explanation.definitionFit: A binding contract is restraining, and two teams drawing are making the score equal.

clue.text: Fantastic escape after vessel overturned

indicators.note: after places the escape behind the overturned vessel
overturned means the vessel is upturned, read in reverse

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
flight is an escape

explanation.surface: A great escape after a boat capsized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns POT into TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest class, excellent, superb.

clue.text: Precisely where the reader may resort for memoirs?

definitions.meaning: exactly, as a portrait captured perfectly

definitions.text: where the reader may resort for memoirs?
definitions.meaning: a reader wanting memoirs turns to a person's biography, their story

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: one goes 'to the life' story of a person for their memoirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness caught exactly is faithful in every detail; and a biography records someone's whole existence.

clue.text: College ultimately cuts organised learning across the board

indicators.note: cuts means the letter goes into the anagram
organised means the letters are put into a new order
ultimately means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A college finally reduces formal study for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges LEARNING; 'ultimately' gives E from College, which 'cuts' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the board means applying to everything, as does on the whole.

clue.text: Elder priest shunning current hosts by turning about

indicators.note: hosts means the cut-down priest takes another word inside
shunning means avoiding, so the current symbol is dropped from the word

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: turning means the word for about is reversed

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A church elder avoids the flow while turning around.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the physics symbol for current; 'shunning' leaves PREST, 'hosts' wraps it round the clue's own 'by' to make PRESBYT, and 'turning' gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder in the early or Presbyterian church, an office of church governance.

clue.text: Toreador whirls, primarily to confuse bull

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the words are used

parts.note: addle means to confuse or muddle

explanation.surface: A bullfighter spins to bewilder the bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' seems the toreador's animal, but here is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for nonsense, and twaddle is silly talk.

clue.text: Those excluded from court amid random jeers

indicators.note: amid means the court abbreviation goes among the letters
random means the letters are put in no set order

explanation.surface: People thrown out of court among scattered jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' gives REJES, and 'amid' slips the court abbreviation in after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejects are those turned down or cast aside.

clue.text: Fraudster making journey back in regret

indicators.note: in puts the reversed journey inside the word for regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: back means the word for journey is reversed

parts.note: a go can mean a journey or trip

explanation.surface: A conman who regrets his trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journey' is a go, as in having a go somewhere; 'back' gives OG and 'in' sets it within the word for regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, a swindler or cheat.

clue.text: Supposed repository of lost car, with black interior

indicators.note: interior means the black letter sits inside the car

parts.note: a limo is a luxury car
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A black-interiored car in a lost property store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' is a noun: lost souls. In Catholic belief this was a place for unbaptised souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo was held to be the borderland where unbaptised souls were kept, a neglected place for forgotten things.

clue.text: Olympian dreams of this mess, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is used

parts.note: to meddle is to mess about with things

explanation.surface: An athlete dreams of this mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympic athletes aspire to win gold, silver or bronze awards for their achievement.

clue.text: Closeness of Jane and Cecily in distress, Neil having left

indicators.note: in distress suggests the letters are troubled into a new arrangement
having left means Neil's letters are taken from the pool

explanation.surface: Two women in trouble after Neil walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' shuffles JANE AND CECILY; 'having left' removes the letters of NEIL from that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacency is the state of being next to something, nearness.

clue.text: Tail of husky walking on air, commonly barking

indicators.note: tail of means the final letter of the word
commonly signals a dropped H, as in casual speech

parts.note: walking on air means very happy

explanation.surface: A happy husky barking as it walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' drops the H of HAPPY as in Cockney speech, giving APPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A yappy dog barks shrilly and persistently.

clue.text: Object added to gallery a very timely gift

indicators.note: added to means the object word is put after the gallery word

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
an end is an object or purpose

explanation.surface: A new artwork added to a gallery's collection arrives just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like an art object; it is END, an aim. THE GODS is the top gallery of a British theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected and welcome help arriving at just the right moment.

clue.text: Tweet greeting bishop in competition

indicators.note: in places the greeting and bishop inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a trophy competition
hi is a greeting
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop's social media greeting during a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweet' reads as a social media post but is a bird's call. RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a short, high bird sound, the kind of chirp a small songbird makes.

clue.text: Charge for using ring on regular basis

definitions.meaning: a fee paid to use a road or bridge
to sound a bell slowly with strokes at even intervals

explanation.surface: A phone subscription charged at a fixed rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A road fee is levied on motorists for passage, and a funeral bell sounds with slow even strokes.

clue.text: Boy participating in gym to improve as an individual

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class

indicators.note: participating in means the boy takes part inside the other pieces

parts.note: to rally is to recover or improve
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad takes up gym lessons for self-improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, school gym; 'participating in' slots the boy in after the R of the rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something oneself rather than through others means acting in one's own capacity.
